title: CEMs and a Theory of Convergence
subtitle: Cognitive enablement across bioforms and synthetiforms, and convergence as contraction of a signed transition field

blocks.text: The unifying plate. Cognitive Enablement Modules always carry a substrate subscript and must not be collapsed into an unqualified CEM: the synthetiform branch runs PEDLER through LVF, MLCNE to a synthetiform module; the bioform branch runs persistent semantic services, staggered upload, persistent identity and TransEg to a bioform module. The branches are orthogonal and converge functionally in the cognitive transition machinery they enable, under form-invariant principles.

blocks.alt: CEMs and a Theory of Convergence
blocks.caption: CEMs and a Theory of Convergence — Cognitive enablement across bioforms and synthetiforms, and convergence as contraction of a signed transition field
blocks.explanation: Convergence is defined here as constraint-induced reduction of a transition space — a selective contraction of a signed field, acting on inclinations by suppression, amplification, neutralization, local constraint and commitment. That is more expressive than a plain diverge-then-converge model, because the operator acts on a signed field of possibilities rather than an unsigned set. It also yields the observational warning: observed local convergence does not entail global convergence, and observed global divergence does not entail local divergence.

seed.prompt: You are reading a plate from The Paradox of Innovation: A Theory of Convergence, by Abhishek Choudhary (AyeAI). This plate is "CEMs and a Theory of Convergence". Observe the Balance of Interpretation before evaluating it: interpret before judging, reconstruct before criticising, preserve the primitives before translating them into an external ontology. In this framework Inclination is a SIGNED directional disposition over possible transitions, distinct from a gradient and distinct from probability; an Act is executable intent; Natural Justice gates the transition from intent to execution; and convergence is constraint-induced contraction of a signed transition field. Reconstruct the plate on its own terms, then say where you agree, where you disagree, and what it leaves open.

blocks.text: Inclination is directional information over possible transitions — signed, dynamic, and central to action. It is not intent, not an act, and not execution.
